 Alperen Şengün had a monster 43 points (17-of-24 FGs, 8-of-12 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block and a three in the 125-118 win over the Jazz on Friday.
 Şengün took advantage of the Jazz’s center situation, or lack thereof. He was a monster in this game, and the Jazz had no answers for him at all. He won’t be this good every night, but he had a great performance this season. He is shooting way over what he’s shot at any point in his career from the 3PT line, so that should come down a bit, but he’s having a career at this point and with Durant taking more of a step back, there is a lot more sustainability with what he’s doing.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Alperen Şengün 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #28 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Alperen Şengün produced 19 points (8-of-14 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), 13 rebounds, nine assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors. 
 In 10 games this season, Şengün has recorded six double-doubles and one triple-double. His fantasy value has also been boosted by improved efficiency, with the Rockets center shooting over 50 percent from the field and posting higher averages in points, rebounds, and assists. Turnovers can still be an issue for Şengün on occasion, but he committed just two against the Warriors. 
 Alperen Şengün 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #28 
 Alperen Şengün finished Monday’s win over the Nuggets with 20 points (9-of-17 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), 12 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer. 
 Like Kevin Durant, Şengün finished Monday’s victory two assists shy of a triple-double. The Rockets center held his own against three-time NBA MVP Nikola Jokić, playing efficient basketball as both a scorer and a playmaker. Şengün is closing in on first-round value in 12-team leagues, a few spots ahead of his preseason ADP (18). While some may consider selling high, they should also consider that this may be who Şengün is at this point in his career and hold onto him. 
 Alperen Şengün 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #28 
 Alperen Şengün accounted for 17 points (5-of-15 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), 12 rebounds, 10 assists and three blocks in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 Şengün, who has recorded three double-doubles this season, notched his first triple-double on Wednesday. He didn’t shoot the ball well, but the Rockets center is shooting 54.1 percent from the field this season. This has been an encouraging start for Şengün, whether you’re talking category or points leagues. 
 Alperen Şengün 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #28 
 Alperen Şengün finished Monday’s win over the Celtics with 26 points (12-of-15 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, 10 assists, two steals, two blocks and one three-pointer. 
 The Celtics played three centers in Monday’s game, and none had an answer for Şengün defensively. The Rockets center shot 75 percent from the field and committed one turnover in his most efficient outing of the season. Recording his third double-double of the season, Şengün finished three rebounds shy of a triple-double. Through eight games, he’s outperforming his ADP, providing first-round value in nine-cat formats. 
 Alperen Şengün 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #28 
 Alperen Şengün finished Saturday’s win over the Thunder with 16 points (6-of-17 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), nine rebounds, nine assists and one block. 
 Şengün returned to the Rockets lineup after sitting out Friday’s loss to the Mavericks with a sore back. He played 33 minutes and finished one rebound and one assist shy of a triple-double. Turnovers can still be an issue for Şengün at times, but he’s gotten off to a good start this season. Clint Capela, who started on Friday, recorded four rebounds and two assists in 10 minutes.

 Darryn Peterson put up 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, a block, and four 3-pointers in the 125-118 loss to the Rockets on Friday. 
 The Jazz have let Darryn Peterson go, and we’ve really started to see the Kansas version of Darryn Peterson come into fruition. He has started to carry more of the offense and it’s been looking good for the Jazz. They’ve been in more games, and the team really flows well.  Josh Giddey had 15 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), 10 rebounds, 14 assists, three blocks and three three-pointers against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Giddey’s triple-double was his first of the season and his 21st since joining the Bulls. Only Michael Jordan (28) has more in franchise history. Giddey has made at least 44 percent of his attempts in four consecutive games after an early season shooting slump. He and the Bulls will face the Timberwolves on Saturday.

 Kevin Durant had 22 points (5-of-14 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Jazz on Friday. 
 Durant has been taking a bit of a step back this season, which is remarkable given his age that he’s still averaging 20 points per game. The shot attempts have gone down, the efficiency has gone down, the assists are down, and it’s hard to imagine that it will come back to what it was last season. It’s a good thing for Houston that they haven’t needed him to be that guy, but it looks like father time is starting to catch up with him.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Tari Eason scored 14 points (6-of-13 FGs), 11 rebounds, two assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Jazz on Friday. 
 Eason got the minutes over Jabari Smith in this game, and he was wreaking havoc in this one. He was in the dunker spots and taking advantage of the Jazz’s lack of a high-level big man defender. It’s not a sign to add Tari Eason but more of a reassurance that he is still a good streamer if you’re looking for rebounds with the potential for a good game.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Norman Powell had 33 points (12-of-19 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in the Bulls’ 125-117 victory over the Hawks on Friday. 
 Powell led the Bulls with 33 points in the overtime victory over the Hawks Friday. The 33-year-old guard helped put the game away with an and-1 that put the Bulls up by five with less than two minutes left in overtime. It was Powell’s second game with at least 30 points this season. The Bulls will take on the Timberwolves on the second night of a back-to-back on Saturday.
